output.summary: No published statement located implies or contradicts Theorem DG (the 19/16 bound), the P_ob exclusion or Theorem K7-D23-RICH. This is a bounded result, not novelty. Lemma by lemma, the new mechanisms are elementary elaborations of published tools. (1) DG-1 extends M-S Lemma 3.4(1)+(2) from two product sets to |Q| sets: a product-set intersection is a union of double cosets, and each double coset is granular. It also uses M-S Lemma 4.1 (a gcd-2 pair has alpha=1 and measure 1/2) and the accepted K62-E3 2-adic chain. (2) DG-3 is Zhu (3.1)+(3.4) specialised (3q↦6ℓ, r↦alpha*, values {1,2,4}). (3) The DG-4 / FG7 step bound is Zhu's (3.1) count for an m-fold intersection, i.e. submodularity of h(α)=log[G:G_α], which is group-characterizable entropy (Chan 2007 Thm 1, after Chan–Yeung 2002) [INFERENCE]. (4) TR is product-set and double-coset set algebra (M-S Lemma 3.2(3); the claim in the proof of Lemma 3.5). (5) CC is a fractional M-S Lemma 3.5 at apex z, with capacities from Zhu Thms 2.2/3.1 (= M-S Props 4.2/4.3) and M-S Lemma 2.2. At theorem level: Theorem DG is a new 2-adic, Kraft-type necessary condition in the K6.2* e_d≥4 residue. It scales M-S's apex-intersection counting (Lemma 3.1 with Props 4.3/4.5: three product sets) to every 3-, 4- and 5-subset of five product sets. The P_ob exclusion combines published local steps (Menon 4.1 / M-S 3.8 / M-S 4.4 equal-measure containments; restriction plus Sun(3) as in M-S Lemma 4.6 Claim 1) with Theorem DG. RICH's chain (LP equality at an unmarked u ⇒ every fibre meeting t meets z ⇒ D_t⊆U_zU_u ⇒ D_t∩D_u=∅ ⇒ exactly balanced VFC count at z) was not found in the sources read. Hand checks [INFERENCE]: none of M-S Prop 3.8, Cor 3.9, Lemma 3.10, Cor 3.11, Cor 3.6, Menon 4.1, X1 or the M-S tuple propositions excludes P_ob or the K6.2* residue. In K7 (a1), Cor 3.9 overlaps RICH only on configurations with an all-1 row. Verdict: elementary elaborations assembled into restricted results that matter only inside the lane, not a consequential tuple-family theorem. Significance is narrow (pattern level), below the 'modest extension' the prior screen gave complete K6.3. Direct Sun instances are Sun(2)–(4) only, all published. The computer-assisted Sun(5)/(6) are retained as transitive imports: through the class reduction and LFC provenance, and for RICH also through the D23-MIX/ROW/E8 packages. RICH erratum-1 removed one direct Sun(6) instance. K6.2* (e_d≥4), the K7 different-vertex residues and full Sun(7) remain OPEN.

theorem_comparison.lane_item: DG-1: subset-intersection and double-coset granularity at d
theorem_comparison.lane_scope: K6.2* (README §5 P0/P1): n_d = 2^e_d·5^h_d·w_d with f_d=0; n_i* = 4·3^f*·5^h*·w_*; n_c = 2·3^f_c·5^h_c·w_c (c∈O, |O|=5). At most one vertex has f≥2 and at most one has h≥1; the w's are pairwise coprime and prime to 30. Residue e_d≥4, e*=2. g_d=1, any markers; alpha_(d i*) is not used. Conclusion: N(Q) = n_d·μ(⋂_{c∈Q}U*_cU_d) ∈ (n_d/2^min(e_d, v2 T*_Q))·Z_{>0}
theorem_comparison.primary: M-S Lemma 3.4(1),(2); Lemma 3.2(1)-(2); Lemma 4.1; proofs of Props 4.3 and 4.5. Zhu Lemmas 2.1(ii) and 3.3. Lane: rules-k7-v1 L4 and the K62-E3 Lemma 3 chain

theorem_comparison.applies: As tools: yes. As a stated result: no
theorem_comparison.reduction: Z_Q is left W*_Q-invariant and right U_d-invariant (the proof of M-S 3.4(2) with V∩W replaced by W*_Q), so it is a union of double cosets W*_Q·x·U_d. M-S 3.4(1) with (U,V) = (W*_Q, U_d) makes each a multiple of |G|/gcd(T*_Q, n_d). The K62-E3 chain gives gcd = 2^min(e_d, v2 T*_Q). M-S 4.1 applied to the inverted pair (c,d) gives μ(U*_cU_d) = 1/2. LFC(b), which is Zhu 3.3, gives μ(L_c) = 1/2. Disjointness (E3 step 3) then gives U*_cU_d = G∖L_c. U_d ⊆ Z_Q gives positivity [INFERENCE: hand mapping]

theorem_comparison.new_vs_previous_screen: M-S 3.4(1), the Prop 4.3 grid, Lemma 4.1 and Zhu 3.3 are newly applied. The prior screen had 3.4(2) and 3.2 for FG

theorem_comparison.lane_scope: Row 1 plus: orientation alpha_(d i*)=1 (the alpha*-family; the alpha-family if alpha*_(d i*)=1). K62-E3 steps 1–2: Σ_F|S_F∩O| = 5n_d/2; |S_F| ≤ 3 by Sun(4) inside U_d; n_d/4 i*-fibres. (a) needs every 4-subset to have capped depth ≤ 4, which is automatic when e_d=4. Conclusion: Σ_{|R|=3} 2^(−r_R) ≤ 19/16 − 2/n_d. Under (a): either ≥2 triples of capped depth ≥4 with values (2,4,4)/(4,4,4), or exactly one triple of capped depth 5 with (4,4,4), τ*=16, e_d≥5

theorem_comparison.reduction: Set (G_i, G_j, G_k) = (U*_a, U*_b, U*_c), with 3q ↦ 6ℓ, r_ij ↦ x_ab, r_ijk ↦ τ*. Then [U*_a∩U*_b : W*_R] = ℓ_c·τ*/x_ab ≤ [U*_a : U*_a∩U*_c] = ℓ_c·x_ac, so τ* ≤ x_ab·x_ac, and over all apexes τ* ≤ x1x2. The Lagrange step of (3.4) gives x_ab | ℓ_c·τ*; since ℓ_c is odd and x_ab is a power of 2, x_ab | τ*. DG-4 is the same count with U*_a∩U*_b replaced by W*_R ⊆ U*_j (equivalently, submodularity of log[G:G_α])

theorem_comparison.lane_scope: (a1) K7: n_i = 6r_i with pairwise coprime r. z: r_z = 2^E·5^Bz·w_z, E≥1. t≠z: r_t = 3^A·5^Bt·w_t, A≥1. Bz·Bt = 0; the five W-vertices are unmarked. significance.definition_of_major: Any one of: a new method; a full resolution of a prominent open case (Sun(7), or Sun(k) for k≥5 in arbitrary groups, with imports that can be checked independently); or a quantitative gain over published results under the same assumptions
significance.overall: Narrow, pattern-level partial progress. Elementary elaborations of published mechanisms are assembled into restricted results that matter only inside the lane. Not major
significance.answer: These are not a consequential new restricted theorem at the level of a tuple family. DG-1, DG-3, DG-4, TR and CC are instances or |Q|-fold extensions of tools in M-S, Zhu and Menon. Theorem DG is a new necessary-condition inequality. The P_ob exclusion and Theorem RICH exclude restricted patterns and depend on alpha-pattern hypotheses. No new tuple family is closed

counterpoints: A search miss is not novelty. Only two new sources were read. MathSciNet, zbMATH, Google Scholar and CNKI were not searched, and unpublished work by Gong or others in Nanjing cannot be excluded

Against over-dismissal: the Kraft-type 2-adic subset count, the P_ob exclusion (P_ob had passed every single-vertex and T-rule test) and RICH's cross-apex transfer from LP equality were not found in the sources read

Against over-claiming: every step is an elementary identity or an instance of a published lemma. The constants 19/16 and the 1/6 balances come from K6.2*/K7 index arithmetic and do not carry over to other settings
DG(b) is conditional on (a). For e_d≥5 the deep-4-subset alternative remains
P_ob covers one pattern only. RICH's S1–S4 survive the local test only, and its theorem depends on alpha-patterns rather than index tuples
Dependence: the computer-assisted Sun(5)/(6) are retained. I did not trace whether RICH's D23-MIX path actually uses a Sun(5) or Sun(6) instance
Correctness rests on written proofs, two CLI model reviews and parent checks; there is no Lean or human review. DG erratum v1 was a real gap repair
All lane items share the LFC, VFC, INV and FG machinery, so they should be presented as one contribution carrying one priority risk
